correctness.rationale: Uniform projective supporting-line intersections and uniform arc phases yield the exact conditional binomial kernel with parameter mu*length/pi^2. Independent power-law lengths give a standard Poisson rare-length process. A conditional variance plus tight-candidate bound controls all short-arc degrees jointly, and a Chernoff bound excludes false low degrees from longer arcs. The continuous image has the displayed intensity, and Stieltjes asymptotics give the fixed-k coefficients. The standalone checker passed direct-geometry and independent quadrature tests; simulations are not mistaken for proof.

value.rationale: The natural global minimum of crossing degrees behaves qualitatively differently from typical graph degrees: its entire extreme-order hierarchy is an explicit Poisson process controlled by the short-geodesic length exponent, despite dependent crossings. The Haar projective instance has a nontrivial Rayleigh-type minimum and exact coefficients for every fixed low degree. This provides a structural rare-event geometry-network statistic rather than a trivial evaluation of one crossing probability.
